title: Compact Session Protocol for SDKs: ergonomic streaming + callable outputs (TS / Py / Go)
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Problem: SDK authors and application teams need a single, minimal envelope for progressive model output that supports: incremental text chunks, structured JSON emissions, tool/function call events, resumable sessions, and a compact compatibility shim for older clients. Existing patterns vary across languages which causes duplicated parsing logic and brittle integrations.

Proposal: Define the Compact Session Protocol (CSP) — a newline-delimited JSON frame protocol with a small set of canonical frame types (meta, delta, structured, tool_call, tool_result, checkpoint, final). CSP is intentionally minimal to ease implementation in TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs while supporting high-throughput streaming and clear upgrade paths for legacy event streams.

Key design goals:
- Minimal surface: single framing envelope and small finite set of types.
- Progressive ergonomics: friendly async/iterator patterns in each language.
- Explicit tool/function call framing so SDKs can surface invocation hooks and transcripts.
- Structured output validation: optional JSON schema URL in meta frames for client-side validation.
- Compatibility layer: a shim that maps older evented envelopes (delta/text/tool signals) into CSP frames without loss.

CSP frame example (one JSON object per line):
{
  \"type\": \"meta\",
  \"seq\": 0,
  \"session_id\": \"s_Abc123\",
  \"schema\": \"https://schemas.redwood.ai/sdk/csp/v1/output.json\",
  \"model\": \"redwood/fast-1.6\"
}
{
  \"type\": \"delta\",
  \"seq\": 1,
  \"session_id\": \"s_Abc123\",
  \"text\": \"The quick brown \\\"\"
}
{
  \"type\": \"tool_call\",
  \"seq\": 5,
  \"session_id\": \"s_Abc123\",
  \"tool\": {\"name\": \"search\", \"args\": {\"q\": \"weather seattle\"}}
}
{
  \"type\": \"tool_result\",
  \"seq\": 6,
  \"session_id\": \"s_Abc123\",
  \"tool\": {\"name\": \"search\"},
  \"result\": {\"hits\": 3, \"snippet\": \"Sunny and 58F\"}
}
{
  \"type\": \"final\",
  \"seq\": 999,
  \"session_id\": \"s_Abc123\",
  \"status\": \"complete\"
}

Compatibility notes: older streaming formats that emitted text chunks and separate tool markers will be converted at the server-side to CSP frames. The SDK compatibility shim will also expose a legacy adapter: e.g., on_stream_text(callback) which wires to delta frames. This allows gradual migration for large customers.

Language sketches (purposefully minimal, complete examples stored in artifacts):
- TypeScript: async iterator pattern returning CSPFrame objects, plus convenience wrappers that reassemble text and surface tool call hooks.
- Python: async generator for async clients and a synchronous iterator for blocking clients; helpers to validate structured frames against provided schema URL.
- Go: channel-based streamer with small Frame enum and a Builder that reconstructs text + tool transcripts.

Migration path for server teams: an opt-in header X-CSP-Version: 1 when streaming; servers will accept older clients and optionally run server-side shim to map legacy event streams into CSP when CSP header present.

Observability: each frame includes seq and session_id to support idempotent replays and deduping. SDKs will emit telemetry events for dropped frames, schema mismatches, and tool-call latencies for integration with Redwood Console tracing.

Testing strategy: unit tests for parser/serializer across languages, fuzz tests for out-of-order frames, load tests with concurrent sessions to validate low-overhead framing, and compatibility integration tests that replay recorded legacy streams and assert CSP-normalized output.
acceptance_criteria: CSP wire format documented and published in SDK spec page
TypeScript SDK implements async iterator and convenience text/structured helpers
Python SDK provides async generator + sync adapter with schema validation helper
Go SDK exposes channel-based Streamer and a small compatibility shim
End-to-end test: legacy event stream converted to CSP and client-side adapters produce identical transcripts
Telemetry events emitted for schema mismatch and tool-call durations
implementation_notes: TS: export type CSPFrame = { type: string; seq: number; session_id: string; [k: string]: any } and provide createStream(url, opts): AsyncIterator<CSPFrame>
Py: AsyncIterator[dict] from aiohttp.ws_connect; provide validate_frame(frame, schema_url) helper using jsonschema or fastjsonschema

Go: type Frame struct { Type string `json:\"type\"` Seq int `json:\"seq\"` SessionID string `json:\"session_id\"` Raw json.RawMessage `json:\"payload,omitempty\"` } and Stream(ctx, r) -> (<-chan Frame, <-chan error)
Backwards compat: server will map older 'text_chunk' events into CSP delta frames and legacy 'tool_start'/'tool_end' into tool_call/tool_result frames
Performance: keep each frame < 16KB by design; encourage clients to batch structured arrays into a single frame when possible
comments: 2025-01-21: Initial proposal drafted. Shared with SDK eng and platform teams for feedback. @Liam Chen volunteered to lead TS implementation.
2025-01-24: Review notes from Design (Maya Patel): prefer explicit 'checkpoint' frame for resumability instead of ad-hoc seq markers — agreed, added checkpoint type.
2025-01-28: Security review request filed (ticket SEC-729); response indicates no new cryptographic requirements but recommends clarity around PII in tool_result payloads.
2025-01-30: Internal API review w/ runtime team. Decision: use newline-delimited JSON for maximum simplicity; binary payloads will be base64-encoded and indicated by 'binary': true flag.
2025-02-02: First TS prototype complete, passing unit tests. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/891
2025-02-04: Python async generator reviewed; suggested adding convenience 'text_stream' adapter to incrementally yield concatenated text. Implementing in follow-up task.
2025-02-05: Go streamer POC spikes show ~6% CPU overhead in tight loops; optimization notes added for reducing allocations in parser.
Follow-ups: add sample migration guide for enterprise customers and run cross-language fuzz tests before release
